messages.text: Help me write my toast for Lena's wedding. My toast for Lena's wedding should tell the story of our canoe trip.

Good evening, everyone. For those who do not know me, I am Maya, and I have been Lena’s best friend since we were six.

Lena is the person who shows up. When my car broke down at two in the morning, she came. When I failed my first exam, she sat on the floor with me and made a study plan. And on our canoe trip, when we lost the map, she laughed so hard that I forgot to be scared.

Omar, you found someone who will always find the way home, even without a map. And Lena, you found someone who makes you laugh like that every single day. I have watched the two of you look after each other for four years, and it is the easiest thing in the world to believe in.

So please raise your glasses. To Lena and Omar, to every trip ahead of you, and to never needing the map.
Help me write answers for my PearX interview. My PearX interview answer on traction should lead with the 1,200 weekly users.

Here are answers you can practice.

Q: What does Tidepool do?
A: Tidepool lets small clinics book patients online, so nobody waits on hold.

Q: What traction do you have?
A: 1,200 weekly users across four clinics, growing 15 percent a month.

Q: Why now?
A: Clinics moved their records online in the last two years, so booking can follow.

Q: Why this team?
A: I ran a clinic front desk for three years, and Iris built clinic software before.
I want my PearX interview answer on why now to mention the records move.

Here is a sixty second opening script.
You: Hi, I am Maya, the founder of Tidepool.
You: We help small clinics fill their calendars without phone tag.
You: Four clinics pay us today, and 1,200 patients book with us each week.
Partner: What would you do with the money?
You: Hire one engineer and reach twenty clinics by summer.
